fire_authority: MAIN only. ddm_sz1 fired nothing and spent nothing ($0).
mechanism: The RX1M semantic section's 8,284 B of fixed fp16 metadata (16 W4 scale arrays + 22 fp16 tensors) is stored as raw interleaved little-endian <f2 and is entropy-coded by nothing: an exponent byte alternates with a mantissa byte and the LZ match distance is destroyed. The encoder groups the two byte planes (all high bytes, then all low bytes) over a frozen region before the container's own Brotli; the receiver applies the exact inverse permutation before any parsing, restoring the F12 body byte-for-byte. Pure SERIALIZATION: decoded values are unchanged. The un-split is free receiver code under rule 118 -- no transmitted table, a single O(n) byte scatter. Versioning uses bit 0 of the RX1M header's existing `reserved` byte, so it costs ZERO transmitted bytes; reserved == 0 keeps today's exact code path (inactive is byte-identity) and unknown bits still refuse.
distortion_claim: d_seg and d_pose are UNCHANGED BY CONSTRUCTION. The decode is bit-exact: nine decoded fields hash identically to the base through the patched receiver, so the rendered frames cannot change. This is a pure rate move.

pointer_context.note: rr4 is 560 B BEHIND the fx1 pointer. The standalone split on rr4 therefore lands ABOVE the pointer and is NOT a shipping candidate. Only the fx2-composed rows beat it.

PRIMARY.caveat: offset 49 is the argmax over offsets 0..400, fitted to this frozen payload. Safe (the un-split is a pure permutation) but it is coder alignment noise, not mechanism.

ALTERNATE_defensible_constant.note: Offset and length taken from the format itself (_OFFSET_BYTES, _fixed_metadata_bytes): zero fitted parameters. 22 B behind PRIMARY. This is the frozen SHIPPED_PROFILE in code.

THIRD.note: Reproduces fx2's r5c -515 B exactly. Offset 41 is _HEADER_BYTES applied to a body whose real prefix is 30 -- misaligned by 11 B. Retained for lineage, not recommended over PRIMARY or ALTERNATE.

NOT_FOR_FIRE.reason: All three are ABOVE the fx1 pointer (+62, +45, +40 B). They are the clean standalone measurement of the lever on the rr4 base and are retained as evidence, not as candidates.

composition.base: ddm_fx2 candidate A (fx2_d1_13x_homog_context), byte-closed AFTER its own fire-order was sealed as BLOCKED
composition.disjointness: fx2 re-encodes the token stream (member tail); sz1 rewrites the semantic section (RX1M prefix). Disjoint byte ranges.
composition.additivity_measured: 0 B interaction on all three profiles: 181161 - 711 - split reproduces the measured archive bytes EXACTLY. The archive is a single ZIP_STORED member, so archive delta == member delta == section delta; the three rr4 rows independently confirm slope 1 across three section lengths.
composition.WARNING: fx2 candidate A has NEVER had a distortion row measured on T4. Firing a composed archive buys TWO answers at once (fx2's token probability model AND sz1's split). If the row misses, the attribution is ambiguous. To separate them, fire fx2 candidate A alone first, or accept the joint result.

PRE_FIRE_STEPS: 1. Re-pin the runtime tree. The candidate ships with the PATCHED receiver at <receiver_tree>/runtime/residual_archive.py. The archive and its runtime are ONE object: an archive with reserved bit 0 set will be REFUSED by any unpatched receiver (that is the fail-closed design, not a bug).

2. Entry-point smoke: run the real inflate.sh / parse-back on the candidate archive with the patched runtime, in a clean environment. This arm validated the receiver through read_residual_archive, NOT through a full inflate. The un-split runs before parsing and restores the body byte-exactly, so risk is low but NOT zero.

3. Re-derive the decoded token field sha256 from the parse-back and confirm it equals 9ba2e52b3096585895970066b389bf1261ebc203d5b828cdea056c13858aea52. This arm MEASURED that the token stream section bytes are bit-identical and the corrector untouched, and DERIVED that the decoded field therefore cannot change; step 2 makes it measured.
4. Confirm archive.zip and archive.repeat.zip are byte-identical (already verified locally at build time; re-verify after any copy across filesystems).

falsifiers_pre_registered.d_seg_and_d_pose: EQUAL to the fx2-candidate-A row to ALL DIGITS. The claim is decode-identity, so any drift is a REFUSAL, not a regression -- it would mean the un-split did not restore the body and the weights are corrupt.
falsifiers_pre_registered.archive_bytes: exactly 179930 (PRIMARY) / 179952 (ALTERNATE) / 179935 (THIRD). These are MEASURED archive bytes, not projections, so any deviation means the wrong file was fired.
falsifiers_pre_registered.decode_wall_clock: delta ~0 vs the fx2 candidate A row. The un-split is a single O(n) scatter over 8,284 bytes. A delta > 5 s falsifies the cost model and should be reported. NOT measured by this arm.
falsifiers_pre_registered.projected_S: projected_S inherits the fx1 [contest-CUDA] distortion terms and is a PROJECTION. It becomes a score ONLY through an exact eval row. It is not a score claim.

tests: 25 tests in experiments/test_ddm_sz1_semantic_metadata_split.py, all passing, ruff clean. Non-vacuity PROVEN: four injected mutations (inverse planes swapped, split made identity, receiver offset off-by-one, header patch dropped) were ALL caught.
bug_found_and_fixed: set_rx1_reserved wrote byte index 8 (the low byte of hpac_bytes, a section length) instead of index 7 (reserved). Caught by the suite. The shipped archives were never affected -- the builder packs the header positionally -- but the helper would have corrupted a section length. It now re-reads the header and refuses if any other field moved.

hpac_blob.verdict: NOT MEASURABLE -- re-Brotli does not reproduce the shipped length, so the instrument is not calibrated on this section and any delta would measure the parameter mismatch, not the transform

extension_measured_not_shipped.conclusion: The semantic blob is the ONLY one of the three carrying un-entropy-coded fp16 metadata. pd1's corpus-wide serialization prior does NOT generalize across our sections.

overlap_with_mz2: mz2's q3/q4 and FiLM-prune candidates emit an SD1M/SM3R-tagged semantic body that REPLACES the F12/WANS1 body entirely. They are therefore MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with this split, not composable, unless the split is also implemented for the tagged formats. They are also lossy (548-7,991 decoded parameters change) and score-gated NOT_ADMITTED; this split is bit-exact and needs no scorer run.
spend: $0. No Modal, no paid dispatch, no GPU, no n600 scorer job.
